translations.text: Adam, Seth, Enosh.
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared.
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah.
The sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Elishah, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Javan were Elishah and Tarshish, the Kittites and the Rodanites.
And the sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
And the sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
And Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be a mighty hunter on the earth.
And Mizraim fathered the Ludim, the Lehabim, the Anamim, and the Naphtuhim,
and the Pathrusim, the Casluhim, from whom the Philistines came, and the Caphtorim.
And Canaan fathered Sidon, his firstborn, and the Canaanite,
And the Jebusite and the Amorite and the Girgashite.
And the Hivite and the Arkite and the Sinite.
and the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite.
The sons of Shem were Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad and Lud and Aram. And the sons of Aram were Uz and Emol [?] and Gether and Meshech.
And Arphaxad fathered Cainan, and Cainan fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
And two sons were born to Eber. The name of one was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother's name was Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and [?],
and Uzal and Diklah,
and Ebal, Abimael, and Sheba,
and Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Cainan, Shelah.
Eber, Peleg, Reu.
Serug, Nahor, Terah.
Abram, who is Abraham.
And the sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
These are the descendants of Ishmael: Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam.
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema.
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael.

And the sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. And the sons of Jokshan were Sheba and Dedan, and the sons of Dedan were Reuel, Abdeel, Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
And the sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Enoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
And Abraham fathered Isaac, and the sons of Isaac were Esau and Jacob.
The sons of Esau were Eliphaz and Reuel and Jeush and Jalam and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz. And Tamar, Eliphar’s concubine, bore him Amalek.
And the sons of Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
And the sons of Seir were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon and Ezer and Dishan.
And the sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam, and Lotan’s sister was Timna.
The sons of Shobal were Golam, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Jonah. And the sons of Zibeon were Aiah and Anah.
And the children of Anah were Dishon and Oholibamah, Anah’s daughter. And the sons of Dishon were Amran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
And the sons of Asara were Baltan, Azukam, Joikam, and Ukam. And the sons of Dishan were Uz and Aran.
And these were their kings who reigned in Edom before a king reigned over the Israelites: Balak son of Zippor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
And Balak died, and Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.
And Jobab died, and Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
And Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the plain of Moab, reigned in his place. And the name of his city was Gethem.
And Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.
And Samlah died, and Saul from Rehoboth, which was beside the river, reigned in his place.
And Saul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.
And Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, and Hadad reigned in his place. And the name of his city was Pogou, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred.
And Hadad died, and these are the chiefs of Edom: Chief Timna, Chief Gola, Chief Jetheth,
Chief Oholibamah [?], Chief Elah, Chief Pinon,
Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Garsar,
Chief Magdiel, Chief Zaboin. These are the chiefs of Edom.
And these are the names of the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, Asher.
The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, and Shelah. These three were born to him by the daughter of Shua the Canaanite. Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the Lord’s sight, and he killed him.
Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. Judah’s sons numbered five in all.
The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara—five in all.
The son of Carmi was Achar, the one who brought trouble on Israel by acting unlawfully concerning the things devoted to destruction.
The son of Ethan was Azariah.
The sons of Hezron who were born to him were Jerahmeel, Oram, Oqobel, and Ram.
Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, the leader of the house of Judah.
Nahshon fathered Salmon, and Salmon fathered Boaz.
Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse.
Jesse fathered Eliab, his firstborn, Abinadab the second, and Shammah the third,
Nethanel the fourth, and Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, and David the seventh.
Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel—three.
Abigail bore Amasa, and Amasa’s father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb son of Hezron took Azubah as his wife and fathered Jerimoth. These were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Orna.
Azubah died, and Caleb took Ephrath as his wife, and she bore him Hur.
Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.
After this, Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead. He married her when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub.
And Segub fathered Jair, and he had twenty-three towns in Gilead.
Geshur and Aram took the villages of Jair from them, along with Kenath and its towns—sixty cities, all belonging to the sons of Machir, the father of Gilead.
After Hezron died, Caleb came to Ephrathah, and Hezron’s wife Abijah bore him Asdom, the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel, Hezron’s firstborn, were Ram the firstborn, Baan, Oren, and Ozem his brother.
Jerahmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah. She was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram, Jerahmeel’s firstborn, were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada, and the sons of Shammai were Nadab and Abishur.
The name of Abishur’s wife was Abisea, and she bore him Azabar and Molid.
The sons of Nadab were Seled and Appaim. Seled died and had no son.
The son of Appaim was Ishi; the son of Ishi was Sheshan; and the son of Sheshan was Ahlai.
The sons of Ahlai were Ahishama, Jether, and Jonathan. Jether died and had no son.
The sons of Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza. These are the sons of Jerahmeel.
Sheshan had no sons, but only daughters. Sheshan had an Egyptian servant whose name was Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to his servant Jarha, and she bore him Attai.
Attai fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Abed.
Abed fathered Ephlal, and Ephlal fathered Obed.
Obed fathered Jehu, and Jehu fathered Azariah.
Azariah fathered Helez, and Helez fathered Eleasah.
Eleasah fathered Sismai, and Sismai fathered Shallum.
Shallum fathered Jeconiah, and Jeconiah fathered Elishama.
The sons of Caleb, Jerahmeel’s brother, were Mareshah his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah, the father of Hebron.
The sons of Hebron were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema fathered Raham, the father of Jorkoam, and Jorkoam fathered Shammai.
His son was Maon, the father of Beth-zur.
Ephah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez.
And the sons of Jahdai were Regem and Jotham and Gesom and Phalea and Ephah and Shaaph.
Caleb’s concubine Maacah bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
She bore Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, and Saul, the father of Machbenah and the father of Baal. Caleb’s daughter was Achsah.
These were the sons of Caleb, the sons of Hur, Ephrathah’s firstborn: Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim;
Salmon, the father of Bethlamon, the father of Bethlehem; Ari, the father of Beth-gader.
The sons of Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim, were:
Ara, Esi, Amanith, [?], and [?], the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. From them came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.
The sons of Salmon were Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, half of the Manahathites, and the Zorites.
The families of scribes who lived in Jabez: the Agathites, Samathites, and Suchathites. These are the households that came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
These are the sons of David who were born to him in Hebron: the firstborn, Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite, and the second, Daluiah, by Abigail the Carmelite;
the third, Absalom, son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah, son of Haggith;
the fifth, Shephatiah, by Abital; the sixth, Ithream, by his wife Eglah.
These were born to him in Hebron, and he reigned there for seven years and six months. He reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.
These were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, by Bathsheba, the daughter of Ammiel;
and Ibhar, Elishama, and Eliphelet;
and Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia;
and Elishama and Eliada. These were nineteen sons
of David, not counting the sons of his concubines; and Tamar was their sister.
The sons of Solomon: Rehoboam, Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
Jehoram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son, Amaziah his son, Azariah his son,
Jotham his son,
Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
Amon his son, Josiah his son.
And the sons of Josiah were Johanan the firstborn, Jehoiakim the second, Zedekiah the third, and Shallum the fourth.
The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.
The sons of Jeconiah: Assir, Shealtiel his son.
Malchiram and Pedaiah and Sosamou and Nabathias and Shenazzar and Jeconiah.
The sons of Shealtiel: Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister;
and Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed—eight.
The sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah, Jeshaiah his son, Rephaiah his son, Ornan his son, Obadiah his son, Shecaniah his son.
The sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Joel, Beriah, Noadiah, Shaphat, and Saphek—six.
The sons of Noadiah: Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam—three.
The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pedaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Hananiah—seven.
The sons of Judah were Perez, Hezron and Carmi and Hur and Shobal.
And Keriah his son. Shobal fathered Jahath, and Jahath fathered Ahumai and Lahad. These are the descendants of the Zorathites.
These are the sons of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Jabez. Their sister's name was Hazzelelponi.
And Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These were the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem.
And Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
And Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Teman, and Ashtaran. All these were the sons of Naarah.
And the sons of Helah were Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnani.
And Koz fathered Anub and Zobebah. These were the descendants of the brother of Rechab, the son of Harim.
And Jabez was more honored than his brothers. His mother called him Jabez, saying, “I gave birth to one like Jabez.”

And Jabez called upon the God of Israel, saying, “If only you would indeed bless me and enlarge my territory, and your hand would be with me, and you would grant understanding so that I am not brought low!” And God brought upon him everything he asked for.
And Caleb, the father of Achsah, fathered Machir. He was the father of Eshton.
And Eshton fathered Jatrapha [?] and Paseah and Tehinnah, and the father of the town of Nahash, the brother of Eshelon the Kenizzite. These are the men of Rephah.
And the sons of Kenaz were Othniel and Seraiah, and the son of Othniel was Hathath.
And Manathi fathered Ophrah, and Seraiah fathered Joab, the father of Ge-harashim, for they were carpenters.
And the sons of Caleb Jephunneh were Elah and Naam, and the son of Aram was Kenaz.
And the sons of Jehallelel were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Israel.
And the sons of Ezra were Jether, Mered, and Epher. And Jalon fathered Jether, Meron, Jeshma, and Ishbah, the father of Eshtemoa.
And his wife bore Jared, the father of Gedor, Heber, the father of Socoh, and Jekuthiel, the father of Zanoah. These were the sons of Bithiah, Pharaoh’s daughter, whom Mered married.
And the sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, and Dana, the father of Keseah, and Simeon, the father of Jomam; and the sons of Naamah, the father of Keilah: Otarmi, Eshtemoa, and Maacathi.
And the sons of Shimon were Amnon and Rannon, the son of Snana [?], and Tilon, and the son of Jesse was Zokath, and the sons of Zokath.
The sons of Shelah, the son of Judah, were Er, the father of Lecah, and Laadah, the father of Mareshah; and their descendants were Ebdath, Abustan, and Nesoba.
And Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and Saraph, who settled in Moab; and he brought Abethar back to them in Nathukim.
These were potters who lived in Anatim and Gathera. With the king, in his kingdom, they grew strong and lived there.
The sons of Simeon were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Saul.
Shallum was his son, Basan his son, and Asheman his son.
Mazba was his son, Hamuel his son, Zabud his son, Zaccur his son, and Shimei his son.
And Shimei had six sons and ten daughters. Their brothers did not have many sons, and their whole clan did not increase as much as the sons of Judah.
And they lived in Beersheba, Shema, Moladah, and Hazar-shual,
and in Baalah, Baasom, and Tolad,
And in Bethuel and in Hormah and in Ziklag.
and Bethmarah and Cabora, and half of Seousim, and the house of Barua and of Seorim. These were their cities until King David.
And their cities were Eram, Eremon, Tochen, Ashan, and Teken—five cities.
And all their cities, together with the land around their cities, extended as far as Baal. These were their possessions and their allotments.
And Meshobab, Jamlech, and Josiah the son of Amaziah,
and Joel, and Jehu the son of Sabiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,
and Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jaste, Jasuiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Ishmael, and Benaiah,
and Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah.
These were entered by name among the leaders of their families, and their ancestral households increased greatly.
And they went as far as the entrance to Gerar, to the east of Gai, to seek pasture for their livestock.
And they found abundant, good pasture, and the land before them was spacious, peaceful, and quiet, because those who had lived there before were descendants of Ham.

And these men who were recorded by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. They struck down its inhabitants and the Meunites whom they found there, and put them under the ban to this day. They settled in their place because they found pasture there for their livestock.
And some of them, from the descendants of Simeon, went to Mount Seir—five hundred men. Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Jesse, were their leaders.
And they struck down the survivors who remained of Amalek, and they have lived there to this day.

And the sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn—for he was the firstborn, but when he went up into his father's bed, he gave his blessing to his own son Joseph, the son of Israel, and he was not counted in the genealogy according to his birthright—
for Judah was mighty in strength among his brothers and was their ruler, but the blessing belonged to Joseph.
The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Joel: Shimei, and Bebena his son, and the sons of Gog.
The sons of Shimei: Baal his son.
Beerah his son, whom Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria took captive; he was the leader of Reuben.
And his brothers, according to their clan and their divisions in their genealogy: Joel the chief, and Zechariah.
And Bela the son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel, lived in Aroer, Nebo, and Baal-meon.
And to the east he lived as far as the entrance to the wilderness from the Euphrates River, because they had much livestock in Gilead.
And in the days of Saul they made war against the inhabitants, and those who lived in tents throughout all eastern Gilead fell into their hands.
The sons of Gad lived opposite them in Bashan, as far as Salecah.
Joel was the first, Shapham the second, and Janai was a scribe in Bashan.
And their brothers lived in their ancestral households: Michael, Meshullam, Shobai, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Eber—seven.
These were the sons of Abihail, son of Huri, son of Adai, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo,
son of Ahibuz, son of Abdiel, son of Guni,
chief of the ancestral house of those who lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its villages, and in all the surrounding districts of Sharon, as far as all their outer boundaries.
They were registered in the days of Jotham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

The sons of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh had forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty mighty men who carried shields and swords, drew bows, and were trained for war, ready to go into battle.
They waged war against the Hagrites, the Jeturites, the Naphishites, the Nodabites, and the Nabimites.
They prevailed over them, and the Hagrites and all their tents were delivered into their hands, because they cried out to God in the battle, and he heard them because they trusted in him.
They captured their possessions: five thousand camels, two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys, and one hundred thousand people.
For many fell wounded, because the war was from the Lord. They lived in their place until their own captivity.
The half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land of Bashan as far as Baal-hermon and Senir, and on Mount Hermon and in Lebanon. They grew numerous.
These were the chiefs of their ancestral houses: Epher, Jeshi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Igiel—men of great strength, renowned men, chiefs of their ancestral houses.
They broke faith with the God of their fathers and prostituted themselves by following the foreign gods of the land, whose people God had removed from before them.

And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Phanuca [?], king of the Assyrians, and the spirit of Tiglath-pileser, king of Zobah. He took Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh captive and brought them to Halah and to Habor, by the riverbank of Gozan, where they remain to this day.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar fathered Phinehas; Phinehas fathered Abishua.
Abishua fathered Bukki; Bukki fathered Uzzi.
Uzzi fathered Areas; Areas fathered Meraioth.
Meraioth fathered Amariah; Amariah fathered Ahitub.
Ahitub fathered Zadok; Zadok fathered Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz fathered Azariah.
Azariah fathered Jonah; Jonah fathered Azariah. He was a priest in the house of God that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah fathered Amariah; Amariah fathered Ahitub.
Ahitub fathered Zadok; Zadok fathered Shallum; Shallum fathered Hilkiah.
Hilkiah fathered Azariah.
Azariah fathered Seraiah; Seraiah fathered Jehozadak.
And Jehozadak went into captivity with Judah and Jerusalem at the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of Levi according to their families.
Gershon: Libni his son, Jahath his son.
Joah his son, Abdi his son, Zerah his son, Jeatherai his son.
The sons of Kohath: Izhar his son.
Korah his son, Assir his son, Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son.
Assir his son, Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, Saul his son.
The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth.
Elkanah his son, Zophai his son, Nahath his son.
Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, Elkanah his son.
The sons of Samuel: Joel his firstborn, and Abijah the second.
The sons of Merari: Mahli, Nabar, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son.
Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.
These are the men whom David put in charge of the singers in the house of the Lord when the ark was brought to rest.

They served with musical instruments before the tabernacle, the house of the testimony, until Solomon built the house of the Lord in Jerusalem. They took their places in their appointed order for their service.

These are those who took their places, together with their sons: Heman, Samuel’s grandson, descended from Korah, a Kohathite. From the sons of Kohath: Heman the psalm singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel,
son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,
son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,
son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,
son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,
son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.
His brother Asaph stood at his right: Asaph, son of Berechiah, son of Shimea,
son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah.
son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah,
son of Uri, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,
son of Jahath, son of Gershon, son of Levi.
And the sons of Merari, their brothers, stood on the left: Ethan, son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,
The son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah.
son of Amasai, son of Bani, son of Shemer,
son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
And their brothers, the Levites, according to their ancestral households, were assigned to all the work of serving the tabernacle of the house of God.

And Aaron and his sons burned incense on the altar of burnt offerings and on the altar of incense, carrying out all the work of the Most Holy Place and making atonement for Israel, according to everything that Moses, the servant of God, commanded.
And these are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son.
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son,
Zerah his son, Meraioth his son, Amariah his son,
Ahitub his son, Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son.
And these are their dwelling places in their villages within their territories, belonging to the sons of Aaron of the clan of Kohath, for he became a mighty ruler.
They gave them Hebron in the land of Judah and its surrounding pasturelands.
But the fields of the city and its villages they gave to Caleb, son of Jephunneh.
And to the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge: Hebron and Libnah with their surrounding pasturelands, Jattir with its pasturelands, and Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
and Hilen with its pasturelands, and Debir with its pasturelands,
and Ashan with its pasturelands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands, and Bether with its pasturelands.

And from the tribe of Benjamin they gave Geba with its pasturelands, Alemeth with its pasturelands, Labe with its pasturelands, Anathoth with its pasturelands, and Anchos with its pasturelands. All the cities for their clans numbered fourteen.
And to the remaining sons of Kohath, according to their clans, ten cities were allotted from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
And to the sons of Gershon, according to their clans, thirteen cities were given from the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali, and the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
And to the sons of Merari, according to their clans, twelve cities were allotted from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun.
And the Israelites gave the Levites the cities and their surrounding pasturelands.
And they gave by lot, from the tribe of the sons of Judah and from the tribe of the sons of Simeon and from the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, those towns which they named individually.
And the clans of the sons of Kohath had cities within their territories from the tribe of Ephraim.
And they gave them the cities of refuge: Shechem with its surrounding pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer with its pasturelands,
And Jokneam and its pasturelands, and Beth-horon and its pasturelands.
and Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands.
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner and its pasturelands, and Ibleam and its pasturelands, for the families of the remaining descendants of Kohath.
For the descendants of Gershon, according to their families, from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan and its surrounding pasturelands, and Ashtaroth and its pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh and its pasturelands, and Kadir and its pasturelands,
Ramoth and its pasturelands, and Anem and its pasturelands;
and from the tribe of Asher: Mashal and its pasturelands, and Abdon and its pasturelands,
Hukok and its pasturelands, and Rehob and its pasturelands;
and from the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee and its pasturelands, Hammon and its pasturelands, and Kiriathaim and its pasturelands.
And for the remaining descendants of Merari, from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam and its pasturelands, Kedesh and its pasturelands, Rimmon and its pasturelands, and Tabor and its pasturelands.
And along the Jordan at Jericho, west of the Jordan, from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the wilderness and its pasturelands, and Jahaz and its pasturelands,
and Kedemoth and its pasturelands, and Mephaath and its pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead and its pasturelands, and Mahanaim and its pasturelands,
and Heshbon and its pasturelands, and Jazer and its pasturelands.
And these are the sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron—four.

And the sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jemu, Jebam, and Samuel, heads of their ancestral households; and Tul and Anan, mighty warriors according to their lineage. Their contingent in the days of David numbered twenty-two thousand six hundred.
And the sons of Uzzi: Izrahiah. And the sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, all of them leaders.
And with them, according to their lineage and their ancestral households, were thirty-six thousand warriors equipped for battle, for they had many wives and sons.
And their brothers throughout all the families of Issachar were mighty warriors, eighty-seven thousand in all.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Adiel—three.
These are the sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Uri—five, heads of their ancestral households, mighty warriors. Their number was twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
And the sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jerimoth, Abihu, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were sons of Becher,
heads of their ancestral households according to their lineage, mighty warriors. Their number was twenty thousand two hundred.
And the sons of Adiel: Bilhan. And the sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these were sons of Adiel, heads of their families, mighty warriors, seventeen thousand two hundred who went out in force to fight.
And Shuppim and Huppim, and the sons of Shuraya: Shobu, and his son Jather.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Shahar, and Shallum, sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his Syrian concubine bore to him; she also bore Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife for Saphin and Sephon. His sister's name was Maacah, and the name of the second was Zelophehad. Zelophehad had daughters.
Maacah, Machir's wife, bore a son and named him Peresh. His brother's name was Sheresh, and his son was Ulam.
The son of Ulam was Bedan. These are the sons of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh.
His sister Hammoleketh bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Nomee his son, and Zabad his son.
Shuthelah his son, Ezer his son, and Elead his son. The men of Gath who were born in the land killed them because they went down to take their livestock.
Their father Ephraim mourned for many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
He went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son. He named him Beriah, for he said, "He was born at a bad time in my house."
His daughter was Sheerah, and with those who remained she built Lower and Upper Beth-horon. And the sons of Ozan: Sheerah.
And Rephah his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, Tahan his son.
Eladah his son, Ammihud his son, and Elishama his son.
Nun his son, Joshua his son.
Their possessions and dwelling places were in Bethel and its villages, eastward in Gezer and its villages, and in Shechem and its villages, as far as Gaza and its villages.

And as far as the borders of the sons of Manasseh: Beth-shan and its villages, Taanach and its villages, Gilead and its villages, Megiddo and its villages, and Dor and its villages. In these places lived the sons of Joseph, son of Israel.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Jashub, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and their sister Serah.
The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel. He was the father of Zebeth.
Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Sholgam.
The sons of Japhlet: Besechi, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the sons of Japhlet.
The sons of Shomer: Ahi, Rohgah, Obah, and Aram.
The sons of Elam, the brother of Shophar: Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Shophar: Arnaphar and Shual,
and Beri, Imrah, Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Jether, and Beera.
The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Orek, Hanniel, and Raiel.
All these were sons of Asher, all princes and heads of their families, chosen men, mighty in strength, princes and leaders. Their number for battle in war was twenty-six thousand men.
And Benjamin fathered Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, and Aharah the third,
and Nohah the fourth and Rapha the fifth.
And the sons of Bela were Ard, Gera, and Abihud,
and Abishua and Naaman,
and Gera and Shephuphan and Huram and Shuppim.
These are the sons of Ehud, and these were heads of the families who lived in Geba, and they took them captive to Manahath.
Naaman and Ahijah and Gera—he himself is Jeglaam—and he fathered Uzza and Ahihud.
And Shaharaim fathered Moam after sending him away, and Hushim and Baara.
And Adah his wife bore him Jobab and Zibia and Mesha and Malcam,
and Jeush and Sachia and Mirmah. These were heads of the families of Hushim.
And Meoshim fathered Abitub and Elpaal.
And the sons of Elpaal were Eber and Mishael and Shemer; he built Ono and Lod and its villages,
and Beriah and Shema. These were heads of the families who lived in Elam, and they drove out the inhabitants of Gath.
And their brothers were Shashak and Jeremoth,
and Zebadiah and Arad and Eder,
and Michael and Ishpah and Joha, the sons of Beriah.
Zebadiah and Meshullam and Hizki and Heber,
and Ishmerai and Jezliah and Jobab, the sons of Elpaal.
And Jakim and Zichri and Zabdi,
and Elioenai and Zillethai and Eliel,
and Adaiah and Beriah and Beraiah and Shemariam.
The sons of Amariah: Ishpan and Eber and Eliel,
and Abdon and Zichri and Hanan,
and Hananiah and Omri and Elam and Anathothijah and Athin,
And Iphdeiah and Penuel, the sons of Shashak.
Shamsherai and Shehariah and Athaliah.
And Jareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri, the sons of Jeroham.
These were heads of families according to their ancestry, leaders, and they lived in Jerusalem.
The father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon, and his wife's name was Maacah.
His sons were Abdon his firstborn, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, and Nadab,
and Gedor and his brothers, and Zecher.
And Mikloth fathered Shimeah. They too lived in Jerusalem opposite their brothers, together with their brothers.
Ner fathered Kish, Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Ishmael.
Jonathan fathered Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.
And the sons of Micah were Pithon and Melech and Tarea and Ahaz.
Ahaz fathered Jehoaddah, and Jehoaddah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri fathered Moza.
And Moza fathered Binea; Rapha was his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam his firstborn, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were Azel's sons.
The sons of his brother Eshek were Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
The sons of Ulam were strong, mighty men who drew bows, and they had many sons and grandsons, one hundred and ninety. All these were descendants of Benjamin.
All Israel was recorded according to their number in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, together with those living in Babylon because of their sins.
Those who lived in their original holdings in the towns of Israel were priests and Levites who had been assigned to service.
Some of the descendants of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem.
And Uthai, son of Ammihud, son of Amariah, son of Perez, son of Judah.
And from Shelah, Asaiah his firstborn and his sons.
And from the descendants of Zerah, Jeiel and his brothers, six hundred and ninety.
And from the descendants of Benjamin, Shallum, son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah,
and Ibneiah, son of Jeroham, and Elah, son of Uzzi, son of Michri, and Meshullam, son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah.
And their brothers, according to their ancestry, numbered nine hundred and fifty-six. All these men were heads of their families according to their ancestral houses.
And from the priests, Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin,
and Azariah, son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the leader of the house of God,
and Obadiah, son of Jeremiah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah, and Maasei, son of Adiel, son of Ezra, son of Meshullam, and Laamoth, son of Asher.
And their brothers, heads of ancestral houses, numbered one thousand seven hundred and ninety, strong, mighty men engaged in the work of serving in the house of God.
And from the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hashub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, from the descendants of Merari.
And Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Micah, son of Zichri, son of Asaph.
And Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
And the gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers. Shallum was the chief.
To this day they are at the king’s gate on the east. These are the gates of the camps of the descendants of Levi.

And Shallum son of Kore, son of Abiasaph, son of Korah, and his brothers from their ancestral household, the Korahites, were responsible for the work of the service, keeping watch over the tabernacle. They and their fathers were in the Lord’s camp and guarded the entrance.
And Phinehas son of Eleazar was ruler over them before the Lord, and they were with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the gate of the tabernacle of testimony.
All those chosen for the gates numbered two hundred and twelve. These were in their courtyards, and their number [?]. David and Samuel the seer appointed them because of their faithfulness.
They and their sons were responsible for the gates of the Lord’s house, the house of the tabernacle, keeping watch.
The gates were on the four sides: east, west, north, and south.
And their brothers, in their courtyards, came in for seven days from time to time to serve with them.
For the four mighty men of the gates, who were Levites, were entrusted with responsibility for the storehouses and treasuries of the house of God.
They camped there because they were responsible for guarding it. They were in charge of the keys, and every morning they opened the doors of the temple.
And some of them were responsible for the vessels used in worship, for they counted the vessels when bringing them in and counted them when taking them out.
And some of them were responsible for the sacred furnishings, the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the other spices.
And some of the sons of the priests prepared the oil and spices.
Mattithiah, one of the Levites, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with the work of the sacrifices and the high priest’s pan.
And Benaiah the Kohathite, from among their brothers, was responsible for preparing the bread of the Presence from Sabbath to Sabbath.
And these were the singers, heads of the ancestral households of the Levites, appointed to daily service, for they were engaged in the work day and night.
These were the heads of the ancestral households of the Levites, chiefs according to their lineage, and they lived in Jerusalem.
And Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon, and his wife’s name was Maacah.
And his firstborn son was Abdon, followed by Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, and Nadab,
and Gedor, the brothers of Zaccur, Ahio, Zichri, and Mikloth.
And Mikloth fathered Shimeah. These also lived in Jerusalem among their brothers, together with their brothers.
And Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Baal.
And Jonathan’s son Merib-baal fathered Micah.
And the sons of Micah were Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea.
And Baal fathered Joaddah, and Joaddah fathered Alemeth and Azmaveth, and Zimri fathered Moza.
And Moza fathered Banar; Apha was his son, Eleazar his son, and Azel his son.
And Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam his firstborn, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, Amariah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Asiel.
And the Philistines fought against Israel, and the Israelites fled before the Philistines and fell wounded on the mountains of Gilboa.
And the Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, Saul’s sons.
And the battle grew fierce against Saul, and archers with bows found him, and he suffered pain and was in danger from their bows.

And Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest those uncircumcised men come and make sport of me.” But his armor-bearer would not, because he was very afraid. And Saul took the sword and fell on it.
And when his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his own sword and died.
And Saul and his three sons died that day, and his entire household died together.

And when all the men of Israel who were in the encampments saw that Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled. And the Philistines came and lived in them.
And the next day the Philistines came to plunder the wounded, and they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
They stripped him and took his head and his armor, and sent word throughout the land of the Philistines to announce the good news to their idols and to the people.
And they placed his armor in the temple of their god, and placed his head in the temple of Dagon.
And everyone who lived in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul and to Israel.
And all the mighty men of Gilead arose and took Saul’s body and the bodies of his sons and brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh and fasted for seven days.

And Saul died for the lawless deeds he had committed against the Lord, because he did not keep the word of the Lord, and because Saul consulted a medium to seek an answer, and Samuel the prophet answered him.
And he did not seek the Lord, and the Lord killed him and transferred the kingdom to David son of Jesse.
And all Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh.

Even in the past, when Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them in. And the Lord your God said to you, ‘You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.’”

And all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the Lord. And they anointed David king over Israel according to the word of the Lord, which he had spoken through Samuel.
And the king and his men went to Jerusalem, which is Jebus, and the Jebusites lived there in the land.
And the inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You shall not enter here.” But he captured the stronghold of Zion, which is the City of David.
And David said, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites first shall become chief and commander.” And Joab son of Zeruiah went up against them first and became chief.
And David lived in the stronghold; therefore he called it the City of David.
And he built up the city all around, fought, and captured the city.
And David grew greater and greater, and the Lord Almighty was with him.
These were the commanders of David’s forces who supported him in his kingship, together with all Israel, and made him king over Israel according to the word of the Lord.
This is the number of David’s mighty warriors: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, foremost among the three. He drew his sword against three hundred wounded men at one time.
After him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. He was among the three mighty warriors with David at Pas-dammim.
The Philistines gathered there for battle. There was a plot of land full of barley, and the army fled before the Philistines.
He stood in the middle of the plot and defended it, and they struck down the Philistines. The Lord brought about a great deliverance.
Three of the thirty leaders went down to the rock, to David at the cave of Adullam, while the Philistine army was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was then in the stronghold, and the Philistine army was then in Bethlehem.
David longed for water and said, “Who would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem beside the gate?”
The three broke through the Philistine camp and drew water from the well of Bethlehem beside the gate. They took it and brought it to David, but David would not drink it and offered it to the Lord.

He said, “God forbid that I should do such a thing and drink the blood of these men who risked their lives, for they brought this at the risk of their lives.” He would not drink it. These things were done by the three mighty warriors.
Abishai, Joab’s brother, was commander of the three. He drew his sword against six hundred wounded men at one time.
He was renowned among the three, more honored than the other two, and was their commander, but he did not attain to the three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a mighty man. His deeds in Kabzeel were many. He struck down the two sons of Ariel of Benaiah [?]. He also went down and killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day.

He struck down an Egyptian, an imposing man five cubits tall. The Egyptian held a spear like a weaver’s beam. Benaiah went down against him with a club, snatched the spear from the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada did these things, and he had a name among the three mighty warriors.
He was more honored than the three, but did not attain to the three. David placed him over his household.
These were the mighty warriors of the army: Asahel, Joab’s brother; Elhanan son of Dodo, from Bethlehem;
Shammoth the Harorite; Helez the Pelonite;
Ira, son of the Tekoite; Abiezer the Anathothite;
Sibbecai the Hushathite; Ilai the Ahohite;
Maharai the Netophathite; Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite;
Ittai son of Ribai, from the hill of Benjamin; Benaiah the Pirathonite;
Uri from Nekhel; Gaasabiel [?] the Zarephathite;
Azmaveth the Baharumite; Eliahba the Shaalbonite.
The son of Hashem the Gizonite; Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite.
Ahiam son of Sacar the Hararite; Eliphal son of Ur;
Hepher the Mecherathite; Ahijah the Pelonite;
Hezro the Carmelite; Naarai son of Ezbai;
Joel the brother of Nathan; Mibhar son of Hagri;
Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai the Beerothite, the quiver-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah.
Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
Uriah the Hittite; Zabad son of Ahlai;
son of Shiza, from Reuben, a commander over the Thirty;
Hanan son of Maacah; Jehoshaphat the Mithnite;
Uzzia the Ashterathite; Shamma and Jeiel, sons of Hotham the Aroerite;
Jediael son of Shimri and Joha his brother, the Tizites;
Eliel the Mahavite; Jeribai and Joshaviah his son, the Elnaamites; Ithmah the Moabite; Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
These came to David at Ziklag while he was hard pressed by Saul son of Kish. They were among the mighty warriors who helped him in battle,
armed with bows, using both their right and left hands, and slinging stones and shooting arrows. They were from Saul’s kinsmen, from Benjamin:
Ahiezer the chief and Joash, sons of Shemaah the Gibeahite; Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Beracah and Jehu the Anathothite;
Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty warrior among the Thirty and commander over the Thirty; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Zabad from Gederah;
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah from Hariph;
Elkanah, Isshiah, Eliel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;
Joel and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham the Gedorite.

Some from Gad and from the wilderness broke away to join David: strong, mighty warriors who fought in battle, carrying shields and spears. Their faces were like the faces of lions, and they were swift-footed, like gazelles speeding over the mountains.
Ezer was the chief, Obadiah second, Eliab third,
Mishmannah was fourth, Jeremiah fifth.
Attai sixth, Eliel seventh,
Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth,
Jeremiah tenth, Machbannai eleventh.
These were commanders of the army from the sons of Gad, the lesser over hundreds and the greater over thousands.
These were the ones who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it was full throughout all its channels, and drove out all the inhabitants of the valleys, from east to west.
Some of the sons of Benjamin and Judah came to help David.

David went out to meet them and said to them, “If you have come to me in peace, my heart will be with you. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies, acting deceitfully, may the God of our fathers see it and rebuke you.”

The Spirit strengthened Amasa, the commander of the thirty, and he said, “Go forth, David son of Jesse, you and your army! Peace to you, and peace to those who help you, because your God has helped you.” David received them and appointed them commanders of the army.

Some from Manasseh joined David when the Philistines came against Saul in battle. But he did not help them, because the commanders of the Philistines decided against it, saying, “He will return to his master Saul with the heads of these men.”
As he went to Ziklag, Adnah, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai joined him from Manasseh. They were commanders of thousands in Manasseh.
They joined David against the raiding band, for they were all mighty men of strength, commanders over the army.
For day after day they came to David, forming a great army like the army of God.
These are the names of the commanders of the army who came to David at Hebron to transfer Saul’s kingdom to him, according to the word of God.
The sons of Judah, carrying shields and spears: six thousand eight hundred mighty warriors.
From the sons of Simeon, mighty men of strength for battle: seven thousand one hundred.
From the sons of Levi: four thousand six hundred.
Judas was a leader, and with him were three thousand seven hundred of the sons of Aaron.
Zadok was a young man mighty in strength, and there were twenty-two leaders from his father’s household.
From the sons of Benjamin, Saul’s relatives: three thousand. Many of them were guardians of Saul’s household.
From the sons of Ephraim: twenty thousand eight hundred mighty men of strength, men renowned in their ancestral households.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh came eighteen thousand who had been designated by name to make David king.
From the sons of Issachar, who understood the times and knew what Israel should do: two hundred leaders, with all their brothers under them.
From Zebulun, those who went out to battle with every kind of weapon of war: fifty thousand, who came to help David, not empty-handed.
From Naphtali: a thousand leaders, and with them thirty thousand men carrying shields and spears.
From Dan, men drawn up for battle: twenty-eight thousand eight hundred.
From Asher, those who went out to help in battle: forty thousand.
From the other side of the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, with every kind of weapon of war: one hundred twenty thousand.
All these warriors, arrayed for battle, came to Hebron with peaceful intent to make David king over Israel. All the rest of Israel were also of one mind about making David king.
They were there for three days, eating and drinking, because their brothers had made preparations for them.

Their neighbors, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought them provisions on camels, donkeys, mules, and oxen: flour, figs, raisins, wine, oil, and many cattle and sheep, for there was joy in Israel.
David consulted with the commanders of thousands, the commanders of hundreds, and all the leaders.

David said to the whole assembly of Israel, “If this seems good to you and the Lord our God has granted it success, let us send to our brothers who remain throughout Israel, and to the priests and Levites with them in the towns of their holdings, so that they may gather to us.”
And let us bring the ark of our God here to us, for they did not seek it in the days of Saul.
And the whole assembly agreed to do so, for the proposal was right in the eyes of all the people.
And David gathered all Israel, from the borders of Egypt as far as Hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.

And David brought it up, and all Israel went up to the city of David, which belonged to Judah, to bring from there the ark of the Lord God, who sits above the cherubim, over which his name was invoked.
And they placed the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, and Uzzah and his brothers drove the cart.
David and all Israel danced before God with all their strength, with songs of psalms, harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
And they came to the threshing floor of Kelon, and Uzzah stretched out his hand to hold the ark, because the ox tipped it.
The Lord's anger burned against Uzzah, and he struck him down there because he had stretched out his hand to the ark. He died there before God.
And David was distressed because the Lord had broken out against Uzzah, and he called that place Perez-uzzah to this day.
And David was afraid of God that day and said, “How can I bring the ark of God to me?”
And David did not bring the ark to himself in the city of David, but diverted it to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
And the ark of God remained in the house of Obed-edom for three months, and God blessed Obed-edom and everything he had.
And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber, masons, and carpenters, to build him a house.
And David knew that the Lord had established him over Israel, for his kingdom had risen to greatness for the sake of his people Israel.
And David took more wives in Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
And these are the names of those born to him, whom he had in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon,
and Ibhar, Elishua, and Eliphelet,
and Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia,
and Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
And the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, and all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard and went out to meet them.
And the Philistines came and gathered together in the Valley of the Giants.
And David inquired of God, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines, and will you deliver them into my hands?” And the Lord said to him, “Go up, and I will deliver them into your hands.”

And David went up to Baal-perazim, and David struck them down. And David said, “God has broken through my enemies by my hand, like a breach made by water.” Therefore he called that place the Breach of Perazim.
And they left their gods there, and David ordered them to be burned with fire.
And the Philistines came again and gathered in the Valley of the Giants.
And David inquired of God again, and God said to him, “Do not go after them. Turn away from them and leave them near the pear trees.
And when you hear the sound of movement in the tops of the pear trees, then go out to battle, for God will go out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
And he did as God commanded him, and struck down the Philistine army from Gibeon to Gezer.
And David’s fame spread throughout the land, and the Lord caused all nations to fear him.
And he built houses for himself in the City of David, prepared a place for the ark of God, and made a tent for it.
Then David said, “No one may carry the ark of God except the Levites, because the Lord chose them to carry his ark and to serve before him forever.”
And David gathered all Israel in Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the Lord to the place he had prepared for it.
And David gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:
From the descendants of Kohath, Uriel the leader and his relatives, one hundred and twenty;
From the descendants of Merari, Asaiah the leader and his relatives, two hundred and fifty;
From the descendants of Gershon, Joel the leader and his relatives, one hundred and thirty;
From the descendants of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the leader and his relatives, two hundred;
From the descendants of Hebron, Eliel the leader and his relatives, eighty;
From the descendants of Uzziel, Amminadab the leader and his relatives, one hundred and twelve.
And David summoned the priests Zadok and Abiathar, and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.
And he said to them, “You are the heads of the Levite families. Consecrate yourselves and your relatives, and bring up the ark of the God of Israel to the place I have prepared for it.
Was it not because you were absent the first time that your God broke out against us, because we did not seek him according to the prescribed rules?”
And the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves to bring the ark of the God of Israel.
And the descendants of the Levites carried the ark of God with its carrying poles on their shoulders, as Moses had commanded by the word of God, according to what was written.
And David said to the leaders of the Levites, “Appoint your relatives who sing psalms with musical instruments—with harps, flutes, and cymbals—to raise their voices on high with a joyful sound.”
And the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from his relatives, Asaph son of Berechiah; and from the descendants of Merari, their relatives, Ethan son of Kushaiah.

And with them were their relatives of the second rank: Zechariah, Joel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Hananiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Uzziah, the gatekeepers.
And the psalm musicians Heman, Asaph, and Ethan played bronze harps to make the sound audible.
Zechariah, Uzziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Hananiah, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played with harps and Alamoth;
And Mattithiah, Eliphelet, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Uzziah played flutes in Sheminith to strengthen the sound.
And Chenaniah, the leader of the Levites, was in charge of the singing because he was skilled.
And Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.
And Shebaniah, Jehoshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, [?] with trumpets before the ark of God; and Obed-edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers for the ark of God.
And David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the house of Obed-edom with joy.
And when God strengthened the leaders who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

And David was dressed in a robe of fine linen, and all the Levites carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, along with the singers. Chenaniah was the leader of the songs that they performed, and David was dressed in a robe of fine linen.
All Israel brought up the ark of the Lord's covenant with shouts, with the sound of the ram's horn, with trumpets and cymbals, and with music played on lyres and harps.
And as the ark of God was coming into the city of David, Michal, the daughter of Saul, leaned out through the window and saw King David dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.
And he brought the ark of God inside and set it in the middle of the tent that David had prepared for it. And they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
And David finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, and he blessed the people in the name of the Lord.
And he distributed to all Israel, to each person, both men and women, one loaf of bread from the baker and one portion from the roasting pans.
And he appointed some of the Levites as ministers before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to sing aloud, give thanks, and praise the Lord, the God of Israel.
Asaph was the leader, and Zechariah was second to him; Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel played harps and lyres, while Asaph played cymbals.
And Benaiah and Uzziel, the priests, played trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God.
And on that day, at that time, David first appointed Asaph and his brothers to praise the Lord.
Song. Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his name; make his deeds known among the peoples.
Sing to him and praise him; tell everyone of his wonderful deeds, which the Lord has done.
Bless his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek his favor rejoice.
Seek the Lord and be strong; seek his face at all times.
Remember the wonderful deeds he has done, his signs, and the judgments of his mouth,
you descendants of Israel, his servants, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is the Lord our God; his judgments are throughout the earth.
May he remember his covenant forever, his word that he commanded for a thousand generations,
the covenant that he made with Abraham and his oath to Isaac.
He established it as a decree for Jacob and as an everlasting covenant for Israel.
He said, "To you I will give the land of Canaan as your allotted inheritance."
For they were few in number, a small group, and strangers there.
They went from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people.
He did not allow anyone to oppress them, and he rebuked kings for their sake:
“Do not touch my anointed ones, and do no harm to my prophets.”
Bless the Lord, all the earth; proclaim his salvation day after day.
Proclaim his glory among the nations, his wonders among all peoples.
For the Lord is great and highly praised; he is feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are idols, but God made the heavens.
Glory and praise are before him; strength and splendor are in his dwelling place.
Give to the Lord, families of the nations; give to the Lord glory and strength.
Give the Lord the glory of his name; bring offerings and come before him. Bow down to the Lord in the court of his sanctuary.
Let all the earth tremble before him; let the earth be established and not be shaken.
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult, and let them say among the nations, “The Lord reigns.”
Let the sea resound with all that fills it, the trees of the field and everything in it.
Then let all the trees of the forest rejoice, for he has come to judge the earth.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
And say, “Save us, God of our salvation, and deliver us from our enemies, so that we may bless your holy name and glory in your praise.”
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. And let all the people say, “Amen.” And they blessed the Lord.
He left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the Lord's covenant to minister continually before the ark, day by day.
And Obed-edom and his brothers, sixty-eight in all; and Obed-edom, who was a son of Jeduthun, and Hosah were among the gatekeepers.
And Zadok the priest and his brothers, the priests, were before the tabernacle of the Lord at the high place in Gibeon,

to offer burnt offerings to the Lord on the altar of burnt offerings continually, morning and evening, and according to everything written in the law of the Lord, which he commanded the children of Israel through Moses, the servant of God.
And with him were Heman and Jeduthun and the others chosen by name to praise the Lord, for his mercy endures forever.
And with them were trumpets and cymbals, to play the songs of God on lyres; and the sons of Jeduthun were at the gate.
And all the people went, each to his own house, and David returned to bless his household.
And when David was living in his house, David said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of the Lord is under tent coverings.”
And Nathan said to David, “Do everything that is in your heart, for God is with you.”
And that night the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying:
“Go and tell David my servant, ‘Thus says the Lord: You shall not build me a house to dwell in,
for I have never lived in a house from the day I brought Israel out of Egypt until this day; I was in a tent, in encampments.

Wherever the children of Israel went, did I ever speak to any of the tribes of Israel or to its judges, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, and say, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?”’”
And now say this to my servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from behind the shepherds’ folds to be leader of my people Israel.
I was with you wherever you went, and I destroyed all your enemies before you. I made you a house according to the name of the great men who are on the earth.

And now I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and you will plant them there. They will dwell by themselves and no longer be troubled, and injustice will no longer humble them as it did at the beginning
and from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. I subdued all your enemies, and now I will make you increase and establish you, I, the Lord.
When your days are fulfilled and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
He will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will not take my mercy away from him as I withdrew it from those who were before you.
He will be faithful in my house, and his kingdom will endure forever, and his throne will be established forever.
Nathan spoke to David according to all these words and according to this entire vision.
Then King David came and sat before the Lord and said: Who am I, Lord God, and what is my house, that you have loved me forever?
These things were not small in your sight, God, and you spoke concerning your servant’s house for the distant future. You looked upon me in a vision of a man; you exalted me, Lord God.
What more can David add to glorify you? You know your servant.
According to your heart, you have accomplished all your greatness, Lord.
There is no one like you, and there is none besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

And who is like your people Israel, a nation on the earth whom God led, redeeming them as his own people and making his name great and renowned, driving out nations before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt?
You made your people Israel your own people forever, and you became their God.
And now, Lord, may the word you spoke to your servant and concerning his house remain faithful forever, as you said.
Lord, Lord Almighty, God of Israel, may the house of David your servant be established before you.
For you, Lord, have opened your servant’s ear concerning building a house for you. Therefore your servant found the courage to stand in prayer before you.
And now, Lord, you are God, and you have spoken these good things concerning your servant.
Begin now to bless your servant’s house, so that it may be before you forever, for you, Lord, have blessed it; bless it forever.
After this, David struck the Philistines and drove them away, and he took Gath and its villages from the Philistines.
He also struck Moab, and the Moabites became David’s servants, bringing tribute.
David also struck Hadadezer king of Zobah at Hamath, when he went to establish his power over the Euphrates River.
David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand horses, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David dismantled all the chariots, leaving only a hundred of them.
The Syrians came from Damascus to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David struck down twenty-two thousand of the Syrians.
David established a stronghold among the Syrians in Damascus, and they became David’s servants, bringing him tribute. The Lord saved David wherever he went.
David took the gold necklaces that were on Hadadezer’s servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
From Metebath and from Hadadezer’s finest cities, David took a very great quantity of bronze. From it Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the bronze furnishings.
Tou, king of Hamath, heard that David had defeated all the forces of Hadadezer, king of Zobah.

He sent his son Hadoram to King David to inquire about his welfare and bless him, because Hadadezer had been waging war against David and David had defeated him. For Tou was an enemy of Hadadezer. Hadoram had all kinds of gold and silver vessels with him.
David dedicated these to the Lord, along with the silver and gold that he had taken from all the nations: from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.
Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He established a stronghold in the valley, and the Edomites became David’s servants. The Lord saved David wherever he went.
David reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness for all his people.
Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Shavsha was the chief scribe.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and David’s sons were the king’s chief deputies.
After this, Nahash, king of the Ammonites, died, and his son Hanun reigned in his place.

David said, “Let us show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.” David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father, and David’s servants came to the land of the Ammonites to comfort him.

The Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, "Do you think David sent these comforters to you to honor your father in your eyes? Have not his servants come to you to investigate the cities and spy out the land?"
Hanun took David’s servants, shaved them, cut their robes halfway up, and sent them away.
People came and told David about the men, and he sent others to meet them, because they were deeply ashamed. The king said, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow, and then return.”

The Ammonites saw that David’s army had been put to shame. Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver and hired chariots and horsemen for themselves from the Syrians of Mesopotamia and from the Syrians of Maacah and Zobah.
They hired thirty-two thousand chariots, along with the king of Maacah and his army. They came and camped opposite Medeba. The Ammonites gathered from their cities and came to fight.
David heard about this and sent Joab and the company of mighty warriors.
The Ammonites came out and drew up for battle at the city gate, while the kings who had come camped separately in the open country.
Joab saw that they faced him for battle both in front and behind. He selected men from all the young men of Israel and drew them up against the Syrians.
He placed the rest of the army under the command of his brother Abishai, who drew them up against the Ammonites.
He said, “If the Syrians prove stronger than we are, come to our rescue. If the Ammonites prove stronger than you are, I will rescue you.
Be courageous, and let us be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. May the Lord do whatever is good in his eyes.”
Joab and the army with him drew up for battle against the Syrians, and they fled before him.
When the Ammonites saw that the Syrians had fled, they too fled before Joab and his brother Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians saw that Israel had defeated them, they sent messengers and brought out the Assyrians from beyond the River, with Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer’s army, at their head.
David was told, and he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came against them, and drew up his forces against them. David formed his battle line against the Syrians and fought them.
The Syrians fled before David, and David killed seven thousand Syrian chariot fighters and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach, the commander of the army.
When Hadadezer’s servants saw that they had fallen before Israel, they made a covenant with David and served him. The Syrians were no longer willing to help the Ammonites.

The following year, at the time when kings go out to war, Joab led out all the army’s forces and devastated the whole land of the Ammonites. They came and besieged Rabbah, while David remained in Jerusalem. Joab captured Rabbah and destroyed it.

David took the crown of Milcom, their king, from his head. Its weight was found to be a talent of gold, and it contained a precious stone. It was placed on David’s head, and he brought away a very great amount of plunder.
He brought out the people who were in it and cut them with saws and iron axes. David did the same to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then David and his entire army returned to Jerusalem.
After this, war broke out again at Gezer against the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Sippai, one of the descendants of the giants, and defeated him.
War broke out again against the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite. The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam.
War broke out again at Gath. There was a very large man there who had six digits on each hand and foot, twenty-four in all. He too was one of the descendants of the giants.
He taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shamma, the son of David’s brother, struck him down.
These were born to Rapha in Gath. They were all giants, and they fell at the hands of David and his servants.
Satan stood among Israel and incited David to count Israel.
David said to Joab and the commanders of the army, “Go and count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring the result to me so that I may know their number.”

Joab said, “May the Lord multiply his people a hundredfold, and may my lord’s eyes see it, for they are all my lord’s servants. Why does my lord ask for this? Let it not bring guilt upon the people of Israel.”
But the king’s command prevailed over Joab. Joab went out and traveled throughout all the territory of Israel, then came to Jerusalem.
Joab gave David the total count of the people. All Israel numbered one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and Judah numbered four hundred fifty thousand men armed with swords.
But he did not count Levi and Benjamin among them, because the king’s command was abhorrent to Joab.
This matter was evil in God’s sight, and he struck Israel.
David said to God, “I have sinned greatly by doing this. Now take away your servant’s wrongdoing, for I have acted very foolishly.”
The Lord spoke to Gad, David’s seer, and said:
“Go and speak to David, and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I offer you three things. Choose one of them for yourself, and I will do it to you.’”
Gad came to David and said to him, “Thus says the Lord: Choose for yourself.”

Either three months of famine, or three months of fleeing from your enemies while the sword of your enemies destroys you, or three days of the sword of the Lord and death in your land, while the angel of the Lord brings destruction throughout the whole inheritance of Israel. Now consider what answer I shall give to the one who sent me.
David said to Gad, “These three things put me in great distress. But let me fall into the hands of the Lord, for his mercies are very great, and let me not fall into human hands.”
The Lord sent death upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

God sent the angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. While he was destroying it, the Lord saw and relented concerning the calamity. He said to the angel who was destroying it, “Enough! Stay your hand.” The angel of the Lord was standing at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David raised his eyes and saw the angel of the Lord standing between heaven and earth, with his sword drawn in his hand and extended over Jerusalem. David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell on their faces.

David said to God, “Was it not I who ordered the people to be counted? I am the one who sinned and committed these evils. But these sheep—what have they done? Lord God, let your hand be against me and my father’s household, and not against your people to destroy them, Lord.”
The angel of the Lord said to Gad, “Tell David to go up and erect an altar to the Lord at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.”
David went up according to the word of the Lord, which had been spoken in the Lord’s name.
Ornan turned when he saw the king and his four sons hiding with him. Ornan was threshing wheat on the threshing floor.
David came to Ornan, and Ornan went out from the threshing floor and bowed before David with his face to the ground.

David said to Ornan, “Give me this site of yours, this threshing floor, and I will build an altar to the Lord here. Give it to me for its full price in silver, so that the plague may cease among the people.”

Ornan said to David, “Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do what seems good to him. Here, I give you the oxen for burnt offerings, the wood of the carts, and the wheat for offerings. I give it all to you.”
King David said to Ornan, “No, but I will buy it for its full price in silver. I will not take what is yours to offer a burnt offering to the Lord at no cost.”
David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for his site.

David built an altar to the Lord there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called upon the Lord, and the Lord answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering and consumed the burnt offerings.
The Lord said to the angel, “Return your sword to its sheath.”
At that time, when David saw that the Lord had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, sacrifices were offered there.
The tabernacle of the Lord, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offerings were at that time at the high place of Gibeon.
David could not go before it to seek God, because he was terrified by the sword of the angel of the Lord.
David said, “This is the house of the Lord God, and this is the altar of burnt offerings for Israel.”
David ordered all the foreigners in the land of Israel to be gathered, and he appointed stonecutters to cut dressed stones and build the house of God.
David prepared a great quantity of iron for the nails of the doors and the gate, and for the frames, and so much bronze that it could not be weighed.
There were also cedar timbers beyond counting, for the Sidonians and Tyrians brought cedar timbers to David in abundance.

David said, “My son Solomon is a young child, and the house he is to build for the Lord must be great and exalted in name and glory throughout all the earth. I will prepare materials for him.” So David made abundant preparations before his death.
He called Solomon his son and commanded him to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon, “My son, I had it in mind to build a house for the name of the Lord God.
But the word of the Lord came to me, saying, ‘You have shed much blood and fought great wars. You shall not build a house for my name, because you have shed much blood on the earth before me.

Look, a son will be born to you, and he will be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his enemies around him, for his name will be Solomon, and I will grant peace and quiet to Israel in his days.
He will build a house for my name. He will be a son to me, and I will be a father to him. I will establish the throne of his kingdom in Israel forever.’
Now, my son, may the Lord be with you and grant you success, and may you build the house of the Lord your God, as he said concerning you.
May the Lord give you understanding and wisdom and strengthen you over Israel, so that you may take care to carry out the law of the Lord your God.
Then you will prosper if you take care to carry out the commands and ordinances that the Lord commanded Moses concerning Israel. Be courageous and strong; do not fear or be dismayed.

Look, in my poverty I have prepared for the house of the Lord a hundred thousand talents of gold and a million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond counting, because there is so much of it. I have also prepared wood and stones, and you shall add abundantly to these,
to carry out skilled work: stone builders and wood carpenters, and everyone skilled in every kind of work
in gold, silver, bronze, and iron, beyond counting. Now rise and act, for the Lord is with you.”
David commanded all the leaders of Israel to help Solomon his son.

He said, “Is not the Lord with you? Has he not given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into your hands, and the land has been subdued before the Lord and before his people.

Now devote your hearts and your souls to seeking the Lord your God. Rise and build the sanctuary of the Lord our God, to bring the ark of the Lord’s covenant and God’s sacred utensils into the house that you are building for the name of the Lord.”
David was old and full of days, and Solomon his son reigned in his place over Israel.
He gathered all the leaders of Israel, the priests, and the Levites.
The Levites aged thirty and above were included in the count, and their number, counted individually, was eight thousand and thirty men.
Of these, twenty-four thousand were supervisors over the work of the house, and six thousand were scribes and judges.
Four thousand were gatekeepers, and four thousand praised the Lord with the musical instruments that they had made for praising the Lord.
David assigned them to their duties day by day—the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And Gershon, and Ladan, and Shimei.
The son of Ladan, a leader of Israel, and Zetham and Joel.
The sons of Shimei were Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the families of Ladan.
The sons of Shimei were Jahath, Ziza, Joash, and Beriah. These were the four sons of Shimei.
Jahath was the chief, and Ziza was second. Joash and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted together as one ancestral household.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.

The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to be holy for the most holy things, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the Lord, to serve him, and to offer prayers in his name forever.
And Moses, the man of God, and his sons were counted in the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses were Gershom and Eliezer.
The son of Gershom was Shebuel, the chief.
