The son of Eliezer was Rehabiah, the chief. Eliezer had no other son, but the sons of Rehabiah became very numerous.
The sons of Izhar were Saul and Move, chiefs.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, and Jekameam fourth.
The sons of Uzziel were Micah, the chief, and Isshiah, the second.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died and had no sons, but only daughters. The sons of Kish, their kinsmen, married them.
The sons of Mushi were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three in all.

These were the sons of Levi according to their ancestral households, the chiefs of their clans, counted and listed by name, each individually. Those twenty years old and above performed the work of service in the house of the Lord.
For David said, “The Lord God has given rest to his people Israel, and he has settled in Israel forever.”
And none of the Levites carried the tabernacle or any of its equipment used in its service.
For according to David’s last words, the sons of Levi were counted from twenty years old and above.

For he appointed them under the direction of the sons of Aaron to serve in the house of the Lord, in the courts, in the rooms, and in the holy places, and to be responsible for all the sacred things and the service of the house of God,
for the bread of the Presence, the fine flour for the offerings, the unleavened cakes, the baking pan, the dough mixed with oil, and all the measures,
and to stand every morning to bless and give thanks to the Lord, and likewise in the evenings.

And they were responsible for all the burnt offerings presented to the Lord on Sabbaths, new moons, and festivals, according to the prescribed number and the regulations governing them, continually before the Lord.
And they carried out the duties of the tabernacle of the testimony and the duties of the sons of Aaron, their brothers, serving in the house of the Lord.
And he divided the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died before their father and had no sons. Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron, served as priests.
David divided them—Zadok from the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech from the sons of Ithamar—according to their number, their service, and their ancestral households.

Among the sons of Eleazar, more chiefs of leading men were found than among the sons of Ithamar. So he divided them, appointing sixteen men from the sons of Eleazar as chiefs of ancestral households, and eight men from the sons of Ithamar according to their ancestral households.
He divided them by their lots, because there were chiefs of the sacred things and leaders in the house of the Lord among both the sons of Eleazar and the sons of Ithamar.

Shemaiah son of Nethanel, the scribe of the Levites, recorded them in the presence of the king and the officials, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the chiefs of the ancestral households of the priests and Levites: one household at a time from the sons of Eleazar, and one at a time from the sons of Ithamar.
The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, and the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, and the fourth to Seorim.
The fifth, Malchijah; the sixth, Mijamin.
The seventh, Hakkoz; the eighth, Abijah.
The ninth, Jeshua; the tenth, Shecaniah.
The eleventh, Eliashib; the twelfth, Shalakim.
The thirteenth, Huppah; the fourteenth, Jeshebeab.
The fifteenth, Bilgah; the sixteenth, Immer.
The seventeenth, Hezir; the eighteenth, Happizzez.
The nineteenth, Pethahiah; the twentieth, Ezekiel.
The twenty-first, Jachin; the twenty-second, Gamul.
The twenty-third, Delaiah; the twenty-fourth, Maaziah.
This is their numbered order for their service: to enter the house of the Lord according to their regulations, through Aaron their father, as the Lord, the God of Israel, commanded.
And among the remaining sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael, Judaiah, Obadiah.
Of the sons of Abijah, the chief was Isshiah.
Of the sons of Saraisa, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
And of the sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekamiah the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah the first and Jusa the second; and the son of Micah, Shamir.
And Micah’s brother, Isshiah; the sons of Isshiah: Zechariah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi.
Uzziah, his son; Benaiah, his son; and Zaccur and Obri.
Mahli: Eleazar and Kish, his son.
And the son of Kish: Ishmael.
And the sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth. These were the sons of the Levites according to their ancestral houses.

They too drew lots, as did their brothers, the sons of Aaron, before the king, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priestly families and of the Levites—the clans that stood on the same footing as their younger brothers.

Those whom King David and the commanders of the army appointed to the work with the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who sang with harps, lyres, and cymbals; and this was the number of those who performed their work:
The sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Jesiel, the sons of Asaph, at the king’s side.
And the sons of Jeduthun—Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six in all—together with their father Jeduthun, sang thanksgiving and praise to the Lord with lyres.
And the sons of Heman were Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shubael, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanan, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman, who played music before the king according to the words of God, to raise the horn. And God gave Heman fifteen sons and three daughters.
All of them, together with their fathers, sang praises in the house of the Lord with cymbals, harps, and lyres, near the king, Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.
And their number, together with their brothers who had learned the songs of the Lord, all of them skilled, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
And they cast lots for their regular service, small and great alike, the accomplished and those who were learning.
And the first lot fell to Asaph and his sons and his brothers: Joseph first; Gedaliah second—he, his brothers, and his sons, twelve.
The third, Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fourth, Zeri, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fifth, Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The sixth was Bukkiah, with his sons and his brothers, twelve in all.
The seventh: Jesharelah, his sons and his brothers—twelve.
The eighth, Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The ninth, Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The tenth, Shimei, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The eleventh, Azarel, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twelfth, Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fourteenth, Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fifteenth, Jerimoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The sixteenth, Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The seventeenth, Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The eighteenth, Hanani, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The nineteenth, Mallothi, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twentieth, Eliathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twenty-first, Hothir, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twenty-second, Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twenty-third, Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twenty-fourth was Romamti-ezer, with his sons and his brothers, twelve in all.
Among those set apart for the gates, from the sons of Korah, was Meshullam son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
The sons of Meshelemiah were Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Nethanel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
The sons of Obed-edom were Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth, for God had blessed him.
Sons were also born to his firstborn son Shemaiah. They held authority in their father's household, for they were mighty men.
The sons of Shemaiah were Othni, Raphael, Obed, Elzabad, and Ahio; and his brothers, sons who were strong and mighty, were Elihu, Semachiah, and Izbacchus.
All these were sons of Obed-edom. They, their sons, and their brothers were strong and performed their work with strength: sixty-two belonging to Obed-edom.
The sons and brothers of Meshullam were capable men, eighteen in all.
Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had a son, Shimri, for whom they reserved the leadership. Since the firstborn was not among them, his father made him the head.
Hilkiah was the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth. All these sons and brothers of Hosah numbered fourteen.
Their assignment for the gates was determined by lot: the heads were to stand on duty in weekly shifts alongside their brothers and serve in the house of the Lord.
They cast lots for each gate according to their ancestral households, for the small and the great alike.
The lot for the eastern gate fell to Shelemiah. They also cast lots for his son Zechariah, who was wise in counsel, and his lot fell on the northern side.
To Obed-edom fell the southern side, and to his sons the area opposite the house of Assuppim.
At the third threshold, Hosah was assigned to the western side, together with the gate of the [?] at the exit of the road, guard opposite guard toward the east.
The Levites were six each day; on the northern side, four each day; on the southern side, four each day; and at Assuppim, two at a time on rotation.
On the western side there were four, and on the road two at a time on rotation.
This was the allotment of the gatekeepers, from the sons of Korah and the sons of Merari.
The Levites, together with their brothers, were in charge of the treasury of the house of the Lord and the treasury of the most holy things.
The sons of Ladan, the son of Gershom: Ladan [?]; the heads of the ancestral families of Ladan and Gershom: Jehiel,
and Zetham and his brother Joel, who were in charge of the treasury of the house of the Lord.
And Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
And Shebuel, of the descendants of Gershom and Moses, chiefs in charge of the treasuries.
And his brother Eliezer; Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, and Zichri his son.

Shelomoth himself and his brothers were in charge of all the treasures of the Holy of Holies that David, the heads of the clans, the commanders of hundreds and thousands, and the commanders of the forces had dedicated.
These had been taken as plunder from the cities, and some of them had been dedicated so that the work of building the house of God would not lack anything.
The things dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah, and all the dedicated gifts, were in the hands of Shelomoth and his brothers.
Among the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were responsible for the external work concerning Israel, to keep records and administer judgment.

Among the Hebronites, Sadias and his brothers, seventeen hundred valiant men, were responsible for the administration of Israel west of the Jordan River, for all the work of serving the Lord and for the king's work.

Among the Hebronites, Uriah was chief of the Hebronites, together with their clans. In the fortieth year of David's reign, in that census, a man of valor was found among them at Jazer of the Gileadites.

His brothers were valiant men, twenty-seven hundred heads of clans. King David appointed them over the division of Reuben, Gad, and the division of the half-tribe of Manasseh, for all matters concerning God and matters concerning the king.

The Israelites, according to their respective numbers—the heads of clans, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and scribes who kept the accounts and served among the people in all the king's divisions—went out and came in according to the work of each division, month by month, throughout all the months of the year.
The first division, for the first month, was under Jashobeam and Balleel, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
He was from the descendants of Perez and was head of all the commanders of the forces for the first month.
The division for the second month was under Dodai and Dacothi, with Mikloth as leader, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The third commander of the forces, for the third month, was Benaiah, son of Jehoiada the priest, the chief, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Benaiah himself was mightier than the thirty and was over the thirty, the contingent of his division.
For the fourth month there was Asahel, Joab's brother, and after him Zebadiah his son and his brothers. The contingents of his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
In the fifth month, the fifth commander was Shamhuth the Izrahite, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
For the sixth month, the sixth commander was Ikkesh son of Ekgeah the Tekoite, and the contingent of his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
In the seventh month, the seventh commander was Helez the Pelonite, from the descendants of Ephraim, and the contingent of his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The eighth, in the eighth month, was Usak the Ekiesthite [?], a Zerahite, and the contingent of his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The ninth, in the ninth month, was Abiezer from Anathoth, in the territory of Benjamin, and the contingent in his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The tenth, in the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, of Zerah, and the contingent in his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh, in the eleventh month, was Benaiah from Pirathon, from the descendants of Ephraim, and those assigned to him numbered twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth, in the twelfth month, was Heldai from Netophah, son of Othniel, and those assigned to him numbered twenty-four thousand.
Among the tribes of Israel, the leader of Reuben was Eliezer son of Zichri, and of Simeon, Shephatiah son of Maacah;
and of Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel, and of Aaron, Zadok;
and of Judah, Eliab, one of David's brothers, and of Issachar, Amariah son of Michael.
And for Zebulun, Shemaiah son of Obadiah; and for Naphtali, Jeremoth son of Uzziel.
And for Ephraim, Hoshea son of Uzziah; and for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah.
And over the half-tribe of Manasseh that was in Gilead was Iddo son of Zechariah; over the descendants of Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner.
For Dan, Azriel son of Jeroham. These were the heads of the tribes of Israel.
David did not take their number from twenty years old and upward, because the Lord had said that he would multiply Israel like the stars of heaven.
Joab son of Zeruiah began to count the people but did not finish. Because of this, wrath came upon Israel, and the number was not entered in the book of the chronicles of King David.
And over the king’s treasuries was Azmaveth son of Adiel, and over the treasuries of the countryside, in the villages, houses and towers, was Jonathan son of Uzziah.
And over the farmers who worked the land was Ezra son of Chelub.
And over the estates was Shimei the Arimathean; and over the village storehouses of wine was Zabdi son of Shephira.
And over the olive trees and sycamore trees that were in the plains was Baal-hanan son of Gideon, and over the storehouses of oil was Joash.
And over the grazing cattle that were in the valleys was Shaphat son of Adaiah.
And over the camels was Ubias the Ishmaelite; and over the donkeys was Jediah the Merathonite.
And over the flocks was Joaz the Hagrite. All these were overseers of King David’s possessions.
Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, an intelligent man, and himself the chief scribe; and Jehiel son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.
Ahithophel was the king’s counselor, and Hushai was the king’s foremost friend.
And after him, Ahithophel was close to him, as were Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar; and Joab was commander of the king’s army.

David assembled in Jerusalem all the leaders of Israel: the leaders of the judges, all the leaders of the daily divisions serving as the king’s bodyguard, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the treasurers who were over his possessions, the mighty men, and the warriors of the army commanders.

King David stood in the midst of the assembly and said, “Listen to me, my brothers and my people. It was in my heart to build a house as a resting place for the ark of the covenant of the Lord and a footstool for our Lord. For that dwelling I prepared these materials: gold, silver, copper, brass, iron, and much wood.
But God said to me, ‘You shall not build me a house upon which to place my name, because you are a warrior and have shed much blood.’

The Lord God chose Israel from all the nations, and from all Israel he chose Judah to establish his kingdom forever. From the house of Judah he chose my father’s house, and among my father’s sons he desired me to be king over all Israel.
And among all my sons—for the Lord has given me many sons—he chose Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the Lord’s kingdom over Israel.
God said to me, ‘Solomon your son shall build my house and my court, because I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
And I will establish his kingdom forever, if he remains steadfast in keeping my commandments and my ordinances, as he does this day.’

And now, stand before this whole assembly of the Lord and in the hearing of our God: keep and seek out all the commandments of the Lord your God, so that you may inherit this good land and pass it on as an inheritance to your children after you forever.

And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your fathers and serve him with a whole heart and a willing mind, because the Lord examines every heart and knows every thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will abandon you completely.
See now that the Lord has chosen you to build him a house as a sanctuary. Be strong and do it.”
And David gave Solomon his son the plan of the temple, its rooms, its treasuries, its upper rooms, its inner storerooms, and the house of atonement,
and the plan he had in mind for the halls of the house of the Lord and all the surrounding storerooms for the stores of the house of the Lord and the supplies of sacred things,

and for the lodgings of the daily shifts of priests and Levites, for all the work of service in the house of the Lord, and for the storerooms for the vessels used in the service of the house of the Lord.
And the [?] of their weights in gold and silver.
He gave him the weight of the lampstands and the designs of their bases,
and the weights of the tables for the bread of the Presence, of each individual gold table, and likewise of the silver ones,
and of the meat forks, the vessels for offerings, and the gold bowls, and the weights of gold and silver, and of each individual container.
He showed him the weight of the incense altar made of pure gold, and the design of the cherubim, whose wings were spread out and overshadowed the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
David gave Solomon all this in writing from the hand of the Lord, according to the understanding that had been given to him and according to the plan.

And David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or dismayed, because the Lord my God is with you. He will not leave you or abandon you until you finish all the work of service in the house of the Lord. And look, this is the plan of the temple, its rooms, its halls, its upper rooms, its storerooms in the lower rooms, and the house of atonement. This is the plan of the temple of the Lord.”

And the divisions of the priests and the Levites are for all the service of the house of God. With you in every task will be everyone who is willing and skilled in every craft, and the leaders and all this people will be at your command in everything.

And King David said to the whole assembly, “Solomon my son, whom the Lord has chosen for himself, is a young child, and the work is great, because this building is not for a human being but for the Lord God.
With all my strength I have prepared materials for the house of my God: gold and silver, bronze and iron, wood, stones for corners and arches, choice stones, precious gems, and many other supplies.

Moreover, because I delight in the house of my God, I have gold and silver that I dedicated to the Lord. And look, I have given this to the house of my God as an additional gift, apart from what I prepared for the holy house:
three thousand talents of gold from Ophir and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to coat the walls of the temple with them,
by the hands of craftsmen. And who is willing to consecrate himself today to the Lord?”
And the leaders of the clans, the leaders of the children of Israel, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the overseers of the work, and the king’s provincial governors willingly came forward,

and gave for the work of the house of the Lord five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
And whoever had precious stones gave them to the treasuries of the house of the Lord, into the hands of Jehiel son of Gershon.
And the people rejoiced because they had given willingly, for they had willingly offered to the Lord with their whole hearts. King David also rejoiced greatly.
And King David blessed the Lord before the assembly and said, “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, the God of our ancestors, from everlasting to everlasting.
Yours, Lord, are greatness and power and glory and victory and might, for you rule over all that is in heaven and on earth. Before you all kings and nations tremble.
Greatness and glory come from you. You are ruler over everyone, Lord, and ruler over all dominions. In your hand are power and wealth, and in your hand is all-ruling greatness to strengthen everyone.
And now, Lord, we thank you and bless your glorious name.
Who am I, and who are your people, that we have been able to offer all this willingly to you? For everything is yours, and we have given you what belongs to you.
For we are strangers and foreigners before you, as all our ancestors were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, and there is nothing lasting for us.
Lord our God, all this abundance that I have prepared for building a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and everything belongs to you.

And I know, Lord, that you examine hearts and love righteousness. We have willingly offered all this with sincere hearts, and now I have seen your people who are here filled with joy and willing to offer to you.
Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our ancestors, preserve this forever in the minds and hearts of your people, and direct their hearts toward you.
And give my son Solomon a good heart to carry out your commandments, your testimonies, and your decrees, and to complete the preparation of your house.
And David said to the whole assembly, “Bless the Lord your God.” And the whole assembly blessed the Lord, the God of their ancestors, and bent their knees and bowed down before the Lord and the king.

And David sacrificed sacrifices to the Lord and offered burnt offerings to God on the following day: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with their offerings, and abundant sacrifices for all Israel.
They ate and drank before the Lord that day with joy, and they made Solomon son of David king a second time. They anointed him as king for the Lord, and Zadok to the priesthood.
And Solomon sat on the throne of his father David and prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
The leaders and mighty men and all the sons of King David, his father, submitted to him.
And the Lord exalted Solomon from above before all Israel and gave him royal glory such as none of the kings before him had possessed.
And David son of Jesse reigned over Israel for forty years:
seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
And he died at a good old age, full of days, greatness, and glory, and his son Solomon reigned in his place.
And the remaining accounts of King David, from first to last, are written in the accounts of Samuel the seer, the accounts of Nathan the prophet, and the accounts of Gad the seer,
concerning his entire reign and his wealth, and the events of his times that befell him, Israel, and all the kingdoms of the earth.
